d2_sfms_sign.explanation: The two numbers are different estimands on different samples. (1) The raw offsets are MEDIAN differences between all 84 star-forming CG4 galaxies and all star-forming galaxies of each control (1019, 1061, 118), unmatched in mass/rank. (2) The matched value is the MEAN paired difference over only 39 pairs in which BOTH members are star-forming, from the pooled deduplicated galaxy-level match. On those same 39 pairs the median difference is -0.045 and the median of paired differences -0.078 (mean -0.147; Wilcoxon p = 0.26; 15/39 pairs have CG4 above its control). The star-forming CG4 galaxies that enter both-SF pairs have a median residual of +0.015 against +0.015 for all star-forming CG4 galaxies, and the matched star-forming controls sit at +0.060 against -0.041/-0.043/-0.030 for the full control SF populations. Both signs are therefore correct for what they measure; the conflict comes from (i) the small both-SF pair subset, (ii) mean versus median, and (iii) the matched controls being a different (mass/rank-matched, pooled) population than the full control SF samples. Only the raw Control4C offset reaches p < 0.05 (group-bootstrap p = 0.030; Control4B 0.064, RG4 0.59) and the matched contrast does not (p = 0.064); this is not a bug. A fourth ingredient is the mass dependence of the residuals about the FIELD-fitted main sequence: in every control the star-forming galaxies with log M* >= 10.3 sit well below the field relation (median -0.19, -0.21, -0.19) while those below 10.3 sit slightly above it (+0.07, +0.01, +0.07); the 23 massive star-forming CG4 galaxies do not show this depression (+0.00), which drives the positive raw medians, whereas the matched controls of the both-SF pairs are lower-mass than their CG4 partners (16th percentiles 9.29 vs 9.64) and therefore inherit positive residuals.

d3_zheng_shen_class.definition_source: Zheng & Shen (2021, ApJ 911, 105, Sect. 2.3): CGs whose members coincide with a Yang et al. (2007) group are 'isolated'; CGs that are subsets of a richer group are 'embedded systems' and, among them, 'embedded CGs' are the subgroups that do NOT dominate the luminosity of their parent group, sum_i^{Npar} L_i >= 2 sum_j^{Nemb} L_j (Eq. 1), while the remainder, which contribute more than half of the parent luminosity, are 'predominant'; members matched to different groups are 'split'. Paper I (Tricottet+25, Sect. 3.3) states the same: Predominant = 'accounting for half or more of their host group total r-band luminosity' (19 groups), Embedded = 'less than half' (37 groups).
d3_zheng_shen_class.implemented: inherited 'Class' column of data/CG4_Groups.csv (Paper I export); used verbatim by paper_additions.zheng_shen_block, morphology_dominance, host_controlled, identity
d3_zheng_shen_class.verdict: CONFIRMED numerically for the stored labels: median host log M200c is 13.83 for the 19 groups labelled 'Predom' and 13.13 for the 37 labelled 'Embedded' (Table E.2), BUT this CONTRADICTS the definitions: every group labelled 'Embedded' contributes >= 0.51 (median 0.83) of its host r-band luminosity (host richness 5--24), i.e. it DOMINATES the host and is 'Predominant' under Zheng & Shen (2021) Eq. 1 and under Paper I Sect. 3.3, whereas every group labelled 'Predom' contributes <= 0.48 (median 0.31; host richness 13--93) and is 'Embedded'. The two labels are swapped in data/CG4_Groups.csv for all 56/56 non-isolated non-split groups (the 0.5 luminosity-fraction boundary is reproduced exactly: no group is ambiguous). With the correct labels, Embedded hosts (rich groups/clusters) are the massive ones, as the definitions imply. Paper I's Sect. 4.3 prose already carried the inconsistency ('Embedded CG4s ... contributing over half the luminosity of the host').

d5_sigma_v_group_match.interpretation: For Control4B the two matched control sets share only 7/54 control groups (13%) and 0 identical pairs; dropping sigma_v changes the matched-control mean elliptical-satellite fraction by -0.123 and the CG4 side by +0.000, so the shift of Delta from 0.160 to 0.284 comes from which control quartets are selected, not from the CG4 side. In the no-sigma_v set the residual sigma_v SMD is +0.27 (CG4 have HIGHER sigma_v than controls; medians 160 vs 129 km/s). Because Control4B quartets embedded in rich hosts carry high gapper sigma_v, matching ON sigma_v pulls in controls from dynamically hotter (richer, more early-type-rich) hosts, which raises the control elliptical fraction and lowers Delta; matching WITHOUT it selects controls from cooler hosts. With four tracers sigma_v is a noisy covariate (Sect. 2.4), so neither Delta is 'the' answer: the pair of values brackets the Control4B contrast, and the ordering Control4C < Control4B, RG4 holds in both. Note that the no-sigma_v Control4B set is NOT better balanced overall: its redshift SMD grows to +0.25 (from -0.08), so the published with-sigma_v match remains the primary one and the no-sigma_v value a labelled sensitivity.
